subproblem.title: A measure finite on compact sets admits no infinite disjoint family of uniformly heavy sets inside a ball
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Let r ∈ ℝ and c ∈ [0, ∞] with c ≠ 0, and let (D_i)_{i∈ℕ} be Borel subsets of ℝ^P such that D_i ∩ D_j = ∅ whenever i ≠ j, D_i ⊆ B_r(0) and c ≤ μ(D_i) for every i. Then these assumptions are contradictory, i.e. the conclusion is False.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (D : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (r : ℝ) (c : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → c ≠ 0 → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (D i)) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (D i) (D j)) → (∀ i, D i ⊆ ball 0 r) → (∀ i, c ≤ μ (D i)) → False
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces (the finite-mass count), stated for an arbitrary pairwise disjoint family D_i in place of the discs Q_i ∩ B_ρ(z_i), the ball B_r(0) in place of B_{R+ρ}(0), and an arbitrary c ≠ 0 in place of ω_2·ofReal(ρ²).
1. (The common ball has finite measure.) The closed ball closedBall(0, r) of ℝ^P is compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space (isCompact_closedBall), so μ(closedBall(0, r)) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. Every D_i satisfies D_i ⊆ B_r(0) ⊆ closedBall(0, r), hence ⋃_{i∈ℕ} D_i ⊆ closedBall(0, r) and, by monotonicity, μ(⋃_{i∈ℕ} D_i) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, r)).
2. (Countable additivity.) The sets D_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint (D_i ∩ D_j = ∅ for i ≠ j), so μ(⋃_{i∈ℕ} D_i) = Σ_{i∈ℕ} μ(D_i) (measure_iUnion).
3. (The series diverges.) Since c ≤ μ(D_i) for every i ∈ ℕ, Σ_{i∈ℕ} c ≤ Σ_{i∈ℕ} μ(D_i) (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum). Since ℕ is infinite and c ≠ 0, Σ_{i∈ℕ} c = ∞ in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.tsum_const_eq_top_of_ne_zero).
4. (Contradiction.) Combining steps 1–3: ∞ = Σ_{i∈ℕ} c ≤ Σ_{i∈ℕ} μ(D_i) = μ(⋃_{i∈ℕ} D_i) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, r)), so μ(closedBall(0, r)) = ∞ (top_le_iff), contradicting step 1. Hence the assumptions are contradictory, i.e. False. ∎
proof_key_steps: All D_i lie in the compact closed ball closedBall(0, r), whose μ-measure is finite.
Countable additivity: μ(⋃_i D_i) = Σ_i μ(D_i).
Σ_{i∈ℕ} μ(D_i) ≥ Σ_{i∈ℕ} c = ∞ because c ≠ 0.
Monotonicity forces μ(closedBall(0, r)) = ∞, a contradiction.

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the prose. All sets lie in a compact closed ball; measurable disjointness gives countable additivity, and c ≠ 0 makes the constant ENNReal series infinite. Monotonicity contradicts compact finiteness. The argument covers arbitrary real r and c = ∞, uses the hypotheses correctly, and independently formalizes without circular reliance. This supplies the selected parent's final contradiction.

subproblem.title: Comparison of two measures on open subsets of small balls extends to a Borel set
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ and ν be Borel measures on ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)), and let D ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set. Assume μ(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and that every w ∈ D has some ε > 0 such that ν(W) ≤ μ(W) for every open set W ⊆ B_ε(w). Then ν(D) ≤ μ(D).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (D : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → MeasurableSet D → (∀ w ∈ D, ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ ball w ε → ν W ≤ μ W) → ν D ≤ μ D
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces (outer regularity on a small ball, then a countable disjointified cover of the disc), stated for an arbitrary measure ν in place of H²⌞Q_i and an arbitrary Borel set D in place of the disc D_i.
1. (Balls have finite μ-measure.) Let w ∈ ℝ^P and ε ∈ ℝ. The open ball B_ε(w) is contained in the closed ball closedBall(w, ε), which is compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space (isCompact_closedBall). By the hypothesis on compact sets and monotonicity, μ(B_ε(w)) ≤ μ(closedBall(w, ε)) < ∞.
2. (Local inequality on Borel sets.) Fix w ∈ ℝ^P and ε ∈ ℝ such that ν(W) ≤ μ(W) for every open W ⊆ B := B_ε(w). Claim: ν(E) ≤ μ(E) for every Borel set E ⊆ B. Proof: the restriction μ⌞B (Measure.restrict μ B) has total mass (μ⌞B)(ℝ^P) = μ(B) < ∞ by step 1, so it is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P; hence it is weakly regular (MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure), in particular outer regular. Since [0, ∞] is linearly ordered, to prove ν(E) ≤ μ(E) it suffices to prove ν(E) < t for every t ∈ [0, ∞] with μ(E) < t (le_of_forall_gt). Fix such a t. Because E is Borel and E ⊆ B, (μ⌞B)(E) = μ(E ∩ B) = μ(E) < t. By outer regularity of μ⌞B (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt) there is an open set O ⊇ E with (μ⌞B)(O) < t; as O is open, hence Borel, (μ⌞B)(O) = μ(O ∩ B). The set O ∩ B is open (an intersection of two open sets), O ∩ B ⊆ B, and E ⊆ O ∩ B because E ⊆ O and E ⊆ B. By monotonicity of ν and the hypothesis applied to W := O ∩ B: ν(E) ≤ ν(O ∩ B) ≤ μ(O ∩ B) < t. This proves the claim.
3. (Empty case.) If D = ∅, then ν(D) = 0 ≤ μ(D) and we are done. Assume from now on that D ≠ ∅.
4. (Countable subcover.) For each w ∈ D choose ε_w > 0 as in the hypothesis, so ν(W) ≤ μ(W) for every open W ⊆ B_{ε_w}(w). Each ball B_{ε_w}(w) (w ∈ D) is open and contains its centre w (as ε_w > 0), so D ⊆ ⋃_{w∈D} B_{ε_w}(w). Since ℝ^P is second countable, TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable, applied to the family of open balls indexed by the points of D, gives a countable set T of points of D with ⋃_{w∈T} B_{ε_w}(w) = ⋃_{w∈D} B_{ε_w}(w). T is nonempty: a point x ∈ D lies in B_{ε_x}(x) ⊆ ⋃_{w∈D} B_{ε_w}(w) = ⋃_{w∈T} B_{ε_w}(w). Hence T is the range of a sequence (w_l)_{l∈ℕ} of points of D, repetitions allowed (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range). Put B_l := B_{ε_{w_l}}(w_l) for l ∈ ℕ. Then D ⊆ ⋃_{w∈T} B_{ε_w}(w) = ⋃_{l∈ℕ} B_l.
5. (Disjointification.) For l ∈ ℕ let E_l := D ∩ (B_l ∖ ⋃_{l'<l} B_{l'}), i.e. E_l = D ∩ disjointed B l in Mathlib. Each E_l is Borel (D is Borel and every B_{l'} is open; MeasurableSet.disjointed), E_l ⊆ B_l (disjointed_subset), the sets E_l are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed), and ⋃_{l∈ℕ} E_l = D ∩ ⋃_{l∈ℕ} B_l = D (iUnion_disjointed together with D ⊆ ⋃_l B_l from step 4).
6. (Summation.) Fix l ∈ ℕ. Since w_l ∈ D, ν(W) ≤ μ(W) for every open W ⊆ B_l, and E_l is a Borel subset of B_l, so step 2 (with w := w_l and ε := ε_{w_l}) gives ν(E_l) ≤ μ(E_l). By countable additivity of ν and of μ on the pairwise disjoint Borel sets E_l (measure_iUnion) and termwise comparison of series in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum): ν(D) = ν(⋃_l E_l) = Σ_l ν(E_l) ≤ Σ_l μ(E_l) = μ(⋃_l E_l) = μ(D). ∎
proof_key_steps: Every open ball has finite μ-measure, because closed balls of ℝ^P are compact.
On a ball B on whose open subsets ν ≤ μ, outer regularity of the finite measure μ⌞B gives ν(E) ≤ μ(E) for every Borel E ⊆ B.
D = ∅ is trivial; otherwise Lindelöf (isOpen_iUnion_countable) gives a sequence of the balls B_{ε_w}(w), w ∈ D, covering D.
Disjointify the cover inside D into Borel pieces E_l ⊆ B_l with ⋃ E_l = D.
Summing ν(E_l) ≤ μ(E_l) by countable additivity gives ν(D) ≤ μ(D).

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the prose and includes every hypothesis. Compact finiteness makes each restricted ball measure finite, so outer regularity supplies the claimed Borel comparison without requiring ν to be finite. Positive radii give a cover; the empty case, nonempty countable enumeration, measurable disjointification and countable additivity are all justified. The supplied proof independently formalizes without additional mathematical obligations or circular reliance.
